episodes.213560: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon hours on Wednesday (7/8).  The storms produced heavy rain with 1 to 2 inches of rain within an hour, causing flash flooding across portions of Green Bay.
episodes.213681: Thunderstorms that developed over Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of July 8, 2026, produced heavy rain across the area. This resulted in flooding, particularly across portions of Wilson County where numerous roads were reported flooded.
episodes.213779: A line of storms crosses into west central Minnesota on the evening of July 7th. A wind gust of 58 mph was recorded on a personal weather station 2 miles northwest of Beardsley with a number of trees damaged or snapped in the town of Beardsley itself. The Minnesota Department of Transportation weather station 3 miles south southwest of Graceville also recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
episodes.213788: A second round of severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening of July 7 across northern and northeast South Dakota. Peak wind gusts included 72 mph in Akaska (Walworth County), 71 mph at the South Dakota State University mesonet station 10 miles west-southwest of Aberdeen, 70 mph at the South Dakota State University mesonet station seven miles south of Claremont, and 68 mph at the Aberdeen Regional Airport Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) all in Brown County. Hail to the size of quarters was observed 5 miles west of the town of Webster (Day County) and in the town of Selby (Walworth County). ||Heavy rainfall was observed across northeast South Dakota, which resulted in flash flooding and river flooding. 5.18 inches was recorded by the CoCoRaHS observer in Claremont, the COOP observer in Webster observed 4.72 inches, and the automated COOP station at Sand Lake logged 4.39 inches. Many of the COOP and CoCoRaHS observers from in and around Aberdeen and points east in Day, Marshall and Grant counties recorded around 2.50 to 3.50 inches of rainfall. Around 2 inches of rain was recorded by the COOP and CoCoRaHS observers in and around the Watertown area as well. ||Flash flooding struck Aberdeen, stranding multiple vehicles in water near 24th Avenue Northwest (Fairgrounds Road). Streets underwater by as much as 1 foot were reported  primarily on the north side of town and eroding storm sewer infrastructure created a sinkhole at 1st Avenue Northeast and North Pennsylvania Avenue. The Marshall county Emergency Manager relayed that flooding around Newport Colony had resulted in roads under water and washouts. Runoff triggered river flooding along Moccasin Creek, Mud Creek, Willow Creek, the South Branch Tributary of Mud Creek, and the Big Sioux River.
episodes.214206: A stalled frontal boundary in conjunction with a trough of low pressure produced numerous clusters of thunderstorms during the late afternoon into early evening hours. Some storms became severe with damaging winds gusts and hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.214550: Thunderstorms tracked eastward across the Colorado plains during the afternoon and evening of July 8th. A few of the storms produced strong outflow winds with the strongest gust reaching 76 mph.
episodes.214756: A broad area of high pressure shifted sufficiently to allow moisture to creep into Utah, and in combination with strong daytime heating, resulted in daily convection with instances of severe and damaging wind gusts, as well as some flooding.
episodes.214844: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.215277: A subtle shortwave moving across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska on July 8 produced enough lift and instability to initiate thunderstorm development. Thunderstorms produced large hail, strong winds and flooding.
episodes.215487: A stalled frontal boundary across Wyoming and a shortwave moving through brought another day of strong to severe thunderstorms to portions of central Wyoming. Wind gusts over 58 mph were reported in Sweetwater, Natrona, Fremont, Sublette, and Johnson Counties. The strongest wind gust reported was 64 mph at Twenty Mile Hill to the north of Casper in Natrona County.
episodes.215491: A stalled frontal boundary in conjunction with a trough of low pressure produced numerous clusters of thunderstorms during the late afternoon into early evening hours. Some storms became severe with damaging winds gusts impacting portions of the Crystal Coast.
episodes.215984: A multi-cell thunderstorm produced minor thunderstorm wind damage near the city of Enid, OK on the afternoon of the 8th.
episodes.216050: A cold front over the southern Middle Atlantic states dropped into central North Carolina during the evening hours. Scattered showers and storms led to damaging winds and flash flooding across the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain.
episodes.216056: A retreating cold front led to scattered showers and storms during the afternoon and evening hours. Some storms over the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain produced wind damage and hail.
episodes.216105: Weak forcing developed showers and thunderstorms across Central MT. This combined with strong daytime mixing helped produce an isolated severe thunderstorm wind gust east of the Little Belts Mountains.
episodes.216192: Over the course of several days between July 6th and July 9th, an unsettled pattern persisted across the Ohio and Tennessee Valley as a cutoff low meandered across the region. A humid, unstable environment was present throughout this time period with dew point temperatures in the mid 70s and precipitable water values near or exceeding 2 inches. On top of this, relatively weak steering flow in the mid-levels of the atmosphere lead to slow movement of showers and thunderstorms which developed, resulting in localized heavy rainfall amounts and flash flooding. Scattered flash flooding occurred across central Kentucky over the four day period, with severe weather impacts mainly being limited to isolated downbursts from hydrometeor loading in otherwise disorganized cells. However, by the 9th, the ingestion of the cutoff low into broader troughing did provide for slightly stronger wind shear and better storm organization. With a seasonably humid and unstable environment remaining in place, this stronger wind shear did promote a bit more coverage of strong to severe storms, with a couple wind damage reports and a spin-up tornado being observed during the evening and early nighttime hours on July 9th.
episodes.216221: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across mainly East Tennessee on the 7th. These began developing during the late morning hours and continued into the late evening hours before dissipating, producing a few instances of flash flooding.
episodes.216445: There were a few reports of severe weather on July 7th as scattered storms moved through MN in the afternoon and late evening. More widespread storms moved through very late on the 7th and into the early morning of the 8th, but the severe weather environment had weakened by the time they moved through.
episodes.216450: After several days of rainfall in the days leading up to July 8th, the ground had become very saturated and primed for a more substantial rainfall event on the 8th. On this day, a quasi-stationary frontal boundary set up across southern Minnesota and acted as a conveyor belt that repeatedly steered storms over the same areas. The storms also had very slow storm motions, maximizing heavy downpours over the already saturated soils. Total rainfall amounts were around 3 to 4 inches in just 3 to 4 hours, with even heavier amounts close to 5 inches just to the east in Mower County (see entry from NWS La Crosse).
episodes.216490: A ridge of high pressure sat to the southwest of the area, though with moisture streaming up and over the ridge into the region. This brought a day of scattered high based thunderstorms across south central and southeastern Colorado, some of which would go o to produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.216756: July 8th was a second consecutive day round of diurnally driven thunderstorms that developed across southeast Louisiana during the afternoon hours as waves of higher moisture moved through an otherwise typical summertime environment. Strong convection initially affected portions of East Baton Rouge Parish, producing minor damage to several homes in the Westminster area and localized flooding near Coursey Boulevard and Sherwood Forest Boulevard. Additional severe thunderstorms subsequently developed northward toward Pointe Coupee Parish where portions of a sugarcane field was flattened.
episodes.216772: Strong thunderstorms moved from Menominee and Delta Counties onto northern Green Bay, bringing strong winds.
episodes.216775: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front in the late afternoon with up to around 3000 J/kg MLCAPE but less than 20 knots of deep-layer shear.  Storms pulsed briefly stronger with some marginally large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216808: During the very early morning hours on the 8th, a decaying cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving east to southeast across far northwest Kansas produced measured wind gusts up to 66 mph in Cheyenne County.
episodes.216839: Throughout much of the afternoon and evening on July 8th, severe storms moved slowly through northeast Iowa with several inches of rain in some locations. This resulted in isolated flash flooding along with rises into flood stage along portions of the Cedar and Upper Iowa River basins. Additionally, these storms produced severe wind gusts which resulted in scattered instances of tree damage.
episodes.216840: Repeated rounds of storms over portions of southeast Minnesota during the afternoon and evening hours on July 8th resulted in scattered instances of flash flooding during this timeframe. This included a closure of Interstate 90 due to flooding near Austin. The excessive rainfall also resulted in Dobbins Creek near Austin reaching into flood stage. Unrelated to flooding impacts, lightning from these storms struck a house in Winona which started a small fire.
episodes.216861: The beginning of an active monsoon period with a recorded wind gust of 70 mph in Sells that led to downed power lines and a power outage. Additionally, a severe thunderstorm moved off the Rincon and Catalina Mountains into the Tucson metro that caused a flag pole to bend and downed tree branches due to the strong winds.
episodes.216934: A broad upper trough and weak surface low combined with strong heating to result in scattered thunderstorm development across eastern Virginia.
episodes.216959: A few strong storms turned severe and produced marginal reports of severe across western SD.
episodes.216992: Strong heating and low level moisture proved sufficient for isolated to scattered strong storms with gusty winds.
episodes.216993: Scattered slow-moving showers and thunderstorms continued into the early morning hours of July 8th with locally heavy rainfall and isolated flash flooding.
episodes.217161: A very slow moving thunderstorm produced 1-2.5 inches of rainfall in an hour that cause flash flooding south of East Brady on the 7th.
episodes.217257: Storms occurred across a few different sectors of southern MT, with hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter occurring across far SE MT, and winds up to 64 mph across south-central MT.
episodes.217258: Areas of southern MT and northern WY had pockets of storms, with Sheridan County seeing hail up to an inch in diameter and heavy rain.
episodes.217394: Damaging winds associated with isolated strong to marginally severe, mostly afternoon and evening, thunderstorms was observed.
episodes.217395: Damaging winds associated associated with an isolated strong to marginally severe storm impacted West Carrol Parish.
